touches.text: Instance: every device has at least one; a singleton is 0.
The instance folder is a number, eg ~/.cairn/devices/cc/0/. A singleton is 0.
A device may be a singleton or not, but nothing in its code differs by instance.
If Cairn isn't set up, or won't come up, the launcher calls the recovery device directly, not over the bus (7.3.1).

Repo-root bin/ holds only the launcher itself (cairn, cairn.cmd), the one thing on PATH, so it runs even when the package won't import (5.3.2.7). Every shortcut lives in the bin/ of the device or machine it belongs to. Its bin/ plus its bus verbs is what help lists at that level (2.4.11). (Q#12: Akien let CC choose, 2026-11-03; CC kept his walk.)
It holds instances, not classes: one shim per instance. If we have cc 0 and cc 1, two shims are running.

An instance is declared by its folder existing in class-space: cairn/devices/<device>/<instance>/ (one address in two roots). Declared = the folders; running = which of those are in the rack. (Q#18, Akien 2026-11-04)

Code home: launchers/ (bootstrap.sh, the python floor that comes up before anything else) moves into the Recovery device, and superclaude (the CC launcher, 12) moves to the CC device. (Q#24, Akien 2026-11-04: "yes to both")
Owns the CC launcher (superclaude): starts Claude Code with Cairn's session contract, in its own memory-capped cgroup (Claude can OOM the box at ~12-14 GB).
